sentences.text:
This claim petition is filed u/s 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a RTA.
2.

The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 21.02.2024 at about 8.00 p.m, when the petitioner was crossing the Wilsongarden 8th Cross and junction and he was reached infront of Flam Restaurant by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.
At that time all of a sudden a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-02-BS-9496 riding by its rider in a rash & negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner and caused the accident.
Due to the terrific impact the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient and also undergone surgery.
He has spent substantial amount towards his treatment.
The accidental injuries have caused him permanent disablement and also suffered physically and mentally pain and loss of income.

The accident was caused due to rash and negligence riding of the rider of motorcycle, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the vehicle are jointly & severally liable to pay compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
4. The respondent No.1 filed written statement admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of sections 147, 149(2), 134(c), 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the rider of its insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the petitioner was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident and also contributory negligence is more on the part of the petitioner.
It is also urged that there is inordinate delay of 2 days that itself vibrantly discloses that the case is foisted so as to wangle the compensation amount from the insurance company.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the insured vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a rider.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 21.02.2024 at about 8.00 p.m, near Rani Park, Wilson Garden Main road, Bengaluru City, due to actionable negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-02-BS-9496 ?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?

6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1. Ex's.P1 to 18 were marked on his behalf.
Dr.Chidanand.
K.J.C was examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.19 to 21 documents.
The respondent No.1 examined its official as RW.1, through him got marked Ex.R.1 & 2 documents.
The respondent No.1 also examined the Investigating Officer as RW.2.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.1 on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 :
As this issue clinches the whole dispute in controversy, this issue is taken for discussion at the inception for better appreciation of evidence and dissection of materials placed on record.
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation on account of injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident.
Before discussion the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to see the case of petitioner in a nutshell.

9. In order to substantiate the contentions, the petitioner stepped into the witness box and filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P11, being the police documents.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 denied the involvement of the vehicle in the accident and contended that it was falsely implicated to have caused the accident.
Further it is contended that the injuries sustained by the petitioner was not due to involvement of the insured vehicle, but it is due to some other reasons which were not known to this respondent.
It is specifically urged that the insured vehicle is planted in this case.
It is further urged that the petitioner has played fraud by falsely implicating the insured vehicle so as to wangle the more compensation which is not tenable in the eye of law.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.
In support of these contentions, the respondent No.1 has not examined any witness before this Court to prove the same.

Further The learned counsel for respondent No.1 contending that in Ex.P.2 complaint the registration number of the offending vehicle is conspicuously missing, as such the insured vehicle was implicated at the time of filing charge sheet so as to deceive respondent and wangle more compensation amount.
When this being specific and positive contention urged by the respondent No.1, let me analyze the materials placed on record in the light of settled principles of law.
It could be borne out from the Ex.P.2 complaint itself that the accident had happened on 8.00 p.m on 21.02.2024.
Ex.P.2 complaint was filed on 23.02.2024 at about 12.00 p.m.
To put in encapsulated form, soon after the lapse of 2 days from the time of the accident the criminal law was set into motion.
Ex.P2 is filed by Latha who is petitioner's sister.
No doubt in the said complaint the registration of the offending vehicle is not mentioned.
But in the said complaint it is clearly narrated the manner of accident.
Based on Ex.P.2 complaint, the Ex.P.1 FIR was lodged.
It is relevant to note that Ex.P.11 charge sheet was filed as against the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KL-02-BS-9496.

It could be borne out from the Spot mahazar it clearly depicts that the complainant stated that on Mani vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23705765/
3 21.2.2024 at about 8.00 p.m, the petitioner was waiting for cross the road, at that time one unknown motorcycle belongs to Manojkumar, and the said motorcycle rider drove the same with high speed and dashed to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Further in the spot mahazar and sketch it is stated that the accident occurred on the Wilsongarden 8 th cross.
When such is the case while analyzing the case filed under benevolent legislation this Court cannot expect strict proof of the same.
No strict proof of evidence can be expected in claim petition of like nature.
PW.1 during his cross examination had deposed that in FIR the vehicle number is not mentioned.

But in the complaint and FIR it is stated that after the accident, the offending vehicle rider accompanied him and admitted to hospital for treatment and at the time of providing treatment he was given his mobile number.
As per the mobile number the Investigating Officer called to the mobile number and confirmed the accident.
Thereafter the IO has issued notice u/s 133 of M.V.Act to the owner.
On 16.12.2023 the owner of the vehicle replied to the notice.
He admitted that involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
From his evidence it could be culled out there is absolutely no toxic nexus between the respondent No.2 who being the owner of the offending vehicle and the petitioner.
Further it is also not the case of respondent No.1 that there is an active collusion of respondent No.2 with that of petitioner herein.
When such being the case, the question arises in the mind of Court as to on what basis the respondent No.1 is contending that insured vehicle is planted in this petition.
10. The respondent No.1 also examined the Investigating Officer as RW.2 goes to show that the offending vehicle was involved in the accident.

In order to prove the contention urged in the petition with regard to the involvement of the vehicle it is relevant to relied on the decision reported in 2011 ACJ 1261 in case of Oriental Insurance Company Limited v/s Reena Awathi and others Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Alahabad held that, "When motorcycle number was not disclosed in FIR but it was detected during investigation.

entities.text: Oriental Insurance Company Limited v/s Reena Awathi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Investigating officer recorded a finding that the accident was caused by the owner and in possession of owner".
Independent witness produced by the complainant stating that Motorcycle was driven rashly and negligently and hence involvement of the vehicle is proved.

11. On the same point of law it is relevant to relied on the decision reported in 2012 ACJ 2569 in case of Shalini and others V/s Harbhajan and others, wherein it was held "merely non mentioning number of the vehicle in the FIR its not sufficient until and unless evidence to show the involvement of the vehicle is produced and insurance company did not adduced any evidence creating doubt on the involvement of the offending vehicle".

entities.text: Shalini and others V/s Harbhajan and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The principles laid down therein is squarely applicable to the case on hand.
In the instant case on hand also the respondent No.1 and 2 have not led any evidence.
More over the respondent No.2 insurance company has not produced any evidence to show the incorrect involvement of the vehicle.
As such this ratio decidendi is also applicable to the case on hand.

12. Further it is relevant to relied on the decision reported in 2011 ACJ 926 in case of Kusum Lata and others V/s Satbir and others (AIR 2011 SC 1234) wherein it was held that the eyewitness in these types of case is prime importance.

entities.text: Kusum Lata and others V/s Satbir and others (AIR 2011 SC 1234)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further relied on the decision reported in 2018 (2) AKR 407 in case of Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd, Hubli V/s Smt. Indrawwa Gurupadappa Nesur and others wherein also in the above said cited decision the eye witness to the accident had not stated with regard to the registration number.

sentences.text: As such his evidence has to be trusted.
13. It is relevant to note that the FIR was lodged after two days of the accident.
The petitioner clearly stated that the person who caused the accident shifted him to the hospital and assured for expenses of hospital and had given his number.
The mere non tracing of offending vehicle by the police is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioners herein.
The non tracing of the vehicle is just an little set-back to the investigation.

In this regard it is relevant to relied on the decision reported in 2022 ACJ 2003 in case of Janabai and others V/s ICICI Lombard General Ins.Co.Ltd., wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that there was dispute with regard to the involvement of the vehicle.

entities.text: Janabai and others V/s ICICI Lombard General Ins.Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above said decision the Supreme Court laid down that the owner of the vehicle has not filed any complaint regarding false implication of the vehicle then the version of the investigating officer has to be trusted.
In the instant case on hand also the respondent No.2 being the owner of the vehicle has not filed any complaint for false implication.
As such the version of IO in the absence of any contra evidence has to be taken in to consideration.

14. In connected to the facts of the instant case, it is also relevant to relied on the decision of Alahabad High Court reported in 2022 ACJ 2341 in case of Sarita Sharma and other V/s Mohd.
Usman and others, wherein it is held as under :
"Accident - Involvement of vehicle - Contention that FIR was lodged against an unknown truck and site plant also does not mention the registration number of offending truck therefore offending truck was implanted - FIR was lodged within 4  hours of the accident and there was non opportunity for claimants to plant a vehicle in such short time -

entities.text:
Sarita Sharma and other V/s Mohd.
Usman and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Non mentioning of truck number does not weaken the case of claimants as accident occurred at 2.30 a.m, and nobody could have noted the number of truck in the dark of night when it is admitted case that truck ran away from the spot after the accident - Whether offending truck was involved in the accident - Held : yes."
15. Return back to the factual matrix in the instant case on hand also after lapse of 2 days the FIR was lodged and there was no room for the claimants to plant a vehicle in such a short term.
But in the instant case on hand the evidence of RW.2 being the Investigating officer lends helping hand to the petitioner in order to prove the involvement of the vehicle.
16. This Court does not find any toxic nexus between the claimant with that of insured with active collusion with the police authority.
The petitioner has clearly established the factum of involvement of the insured vehicle.
In order to prove the above said fact the petitioners have mainly relied on the Ex.P5 to 8 and 11 documents.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that, there was an rash and negligence riding on the part of offending vehicle.
When such being the case their could not be any negligence attributed to the petitioner for walking on the road which is meant for speeding vehicles in the said road.
As such this Court does not find any rashness or factum of volunteer not fit injuria on the part of petitioner.

sentences.text: Further it is pertinent to note that the respondent No.1 has not made any effort to examine the rider of the offending vehicle before this Court.
From material placed on record it is clearly emanating that the accident happened because of negligence on the part of the motorcycle rider.
Even the charge sheet as per Ex.P.11 is also filed as against the rider of motorcycle.
As such there is no impediment holding that there is a negligence on the part of the rider of motorcycle.
Viewed from any angle this Court does not find any reason to distrust the version of the petitioners herein.
The discussion supra makes it is abundantly clear that the accident occurred solely due to the rash negligent riding of the rider of motorcycle.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 In the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of offending motorcycle.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
19. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
The petitioner has produced his Aadhaar card which is marked as Ex.P.13, as per the above said document wherein his year of birth is reflected as 1974.
This indicates that he was aged (50 years 1 months 1 days) 51 years on the date of accident.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA. No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2024.
Therefore, Rs.16,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
20. As per the medical records and evidence of doctor, the petitioner had sustained the following injuries : Right Proximal tibia fracture.
It is needless to say that the injury is grievous in nature.
The discharge summary Ex.P.12 indicates that the petitioner was taken treatment from 28.02.2024 to 13.03.2024 for a period of 14 days.
During the course of treatment he undergone surgery in the form of : Hibrid External fixator application for right proximal tibia done on 05.03.2024 under SAB.

6 21.

entities.text: Mani vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Chidanand.K.J.C as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total permanent physical disability of 42% for limb and 14% disability to the whole body.

It is elicited during the course of cross examination PW.2 categorically admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and the complaints mentioned in the affidavit are not mentioned in any medical records.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
The petitioner is labour.
He has to use lower limb to his day to day labour work.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 5%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 5%.
22. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:The period of hospitalization of 14 days is proved with a help of discharge summary.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.16,800/- (1,200 X 14) is awarded under this head..
23. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

24. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.66,000/- (16,500 X 4) under this head.
25. MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P16, the petitioner has spent Rs.26,000/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.26,000/- towards medical expenses.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '11'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,08,900/- (Rs.16,500 X 12 X 11 X 5/100) is awarded under this head.

7 27.

entities.text: Mani vs Iffco Tokio Gen Ins Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
28. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES : No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

29. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra nutritious : 16,800-00 food & conveyance charges 2 Pain &
sufferings : 50,000-00 3 Loss of income during laid-up : 66,000-00 period 4
Medical expenses : 26,000-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 1,08,900-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 40,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical and other : - Nil - incidental expenses Total 3,07,700-00 30.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
31. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the insurer and owner of the motorcycle thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.1 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.
Therefore this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
32. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,07,700/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the instant case on hand also the respondent No.1 and 2 have not led any evidence.
More over the respondent No.2 insurance company has not produced any evidence to show the incorrect involvement of the vehicle.
As such his evidence has to be trusted.
13. It is relevant to note that the FIR was lodged after two days of the accident.
The petitioner clearly stated that the person who caused the accident shifted him to the hospital and assured for expenses of hospital and had given his number.
The mere non tracing of offending vehicle by the police is not at all fatal to the case of the petitioners herein.
The non tracing of the vehicle is just an little set-back to the investigation.
But in the instant case on hand the evidence of RW.2 being the Investigating officer lends helping hand to the petitioner in order to prove the involvement of the vehicle.
16. This Court does not find any toxic nexus between the claimant with that of insured with active collusion with the police authority.
The petitioner has clearly established the factum of involvement of the insured vehicle.
In order to prove the above said fact the petitioners have mainly relied on the Ex.P5 to 8 and 11 documents.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that, there was an rash and negligence riding on the part of offending vehicle.
When such being the case their could not be any negligence attributed to the petitioner for walking on the road which is meant for speeding vehicles in the said road.
As such this Court does not find any rashness or factum of volunteer not fit injuria on the part of petitioner.

The petitioner is labour.
